title: sdkenv-provisioning-labplay-notes-draft
summary: Notes for an experimental hands-on lab and minimal SDK environment provisioning path. Targets engineers who will run an internal 60–90 minute session to validate first-run experience, telemetry handshake, and toggles for hosted vs private deployments.
content:
Purpose and audience:
This doc collates the work-in-progress playbook for a short instructor-led lab (60–90 minutes) where attendees get a minimal local SDK experience working against Redwood's hosted sandbox and a simulated private endpoint. Audience: backend+frontend engineers, platform engineers evaluating SDK ergonomics, and solutions engineers running demos.

Goals for the lab: (1) make a reproducible minimal path: from zero to a working request in under 15 minutes on macOS/Linux/WSL; (2) exercise both the high-level SDK (convenience client) and the raw HTTP/REST path; (3) validate telemetry consent flow and opt-out; (4) surface common failure modes and diagnostic steps for first-run; (5) capture a short checklist for shipping a production quickstart.

High-level flow (instructor script):
1) Pre-lab (10m): distribute short env checklist, ensure attendees have Docker (optional), Node 18+ or Python 3.10+, and a personal sandbox API key. Provide a single gdrive link with script and one-line bootstrap.
2) Bootstrap (10–15m): clone the minimal repo, install deps (npm/pip), run ./scripts/bootstrap.sh (shell script sets up .redwoodrc).
3) Run a single request (10m): show the high-level SDK call (one-liner) and then the equivalent curl. Emphasize model selection toggles and streaming flag.
4) Telemetry and config (10m): explain default telemetry_on: true, show how to set REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=false and what telemetry ping looks like (anonymized).
5) Failure modes (10–15m): deliberately break auth, simulate network error, toggle to private endpoint.
6) Extension challenge (remaining time): add streaming handler; add a local cache prefix; swap to an internally hosted docker model that simulates lower throughput to show fallback.

Minimal .redwoodrc (proposal):
- api_key: uses env var REDWOOD_API_KEY or ~/.redwood/api_key
- endpoint: https://api.sandbox.redwood.ai (switchable to private endpoint in labs)
- default_model: redwood-mini-1
- telemetry_on: true
- telemetry_anonymize: true
- prefer_streaming: false
Rationale: single file that exercises both hosted and private toggles and helps demos replicate real config flow.

Quick commands (one-line cheat sheet):
- bootstrap: git clone ... && ./scripts/bootstrap.sh
- run node quickstart: NODE_ENV=dev node quickstart.js
- run python quickstart: REDWOOD_API_KEY=... python quickstart.py
- curl: curl -X POST $ENDPOINT/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'

Suggested quickstart snippets (plain text examples attendees will type):
- Node minimal: const rw = require('@redwood/sdk'); await rw.generate({model: 'redwood-mini-1', prompt: 'Summarize this file.'});
- Python minimal: from redwood import Client; c = Client(); c.generate('Summarize this file', model='redwood-mini-1')
- Curl streaming (SSE pseudo): curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" $ENDPOINT/stream ... (in lab show how to handle partial tokens in the client)

Telemetry contract (internal details for instructors):
- On first run, SDK attempts a non-blocking POST to telemetry.redwood.ai/ping with sha256(client_uuid + sdk_version) and runtime metadata (os, node/python version) only when telemetry_on=true. No prompt content is ever sent. If telemetry_on=false explicit env var, skip the call.
- Instructor note: show Network tab in browser devtools or Wireshark on localhost to demonstrate the ping.

Test harness and CI notes:
- Add a lightweight smoke test that runs against the sandbox: tests/smoke/test_quickstart.py (pytest) and tests/smoke/test_quickstart.js (mocha).
- CI should use a sandbox key scoped to smoke tests and rotate monthly. Mark tests as flaky if sandbox is slow; include retry logic.

Common first-run pain points and remediation:
- Missing API key -> clear error message: "REDWOOD_API_KEY not set. See https://.../quickstart"; include a sample 'how to get a sandbox key' link in the error.
- Proxy and corporate networks -> provide instructions to set REDWOOD_ENDPOINT and HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY.
- Streaming partial tokens cause confusion -> include an appendix with small streaming consumer example and how to debounce UI updates.

Lab artifacts to produce by EOD:
- condensed one-page cheat sheet for attendees (printable)
- a single-file quickstart in Node and Python under /examples/minimal/quickstart.{js,py}
- scripts/bootstrap.sh that creates ~/.redwoodrc if missing and inserts placeholder values
- smoke tests wired into CI job pipeline with a sandbox key secret

Open questions (for follow-up):
- Should default telemetry be on or off for internal labs? (privacy vs observability tradeoff)
- What exact permissions should sandbox API keys have for public CI? read-only generation? throttled?
- Do we include a prebuilt Docker image for private-mode simulation or keep everything npm/pip?

References and links for the instructor:
- internal guide: CON-1234 (telemetry design doc)
- lab issue: JIRA-DEVX-78 (hts: bootstrap script and smoke tests)
- example PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-protos/pull/56 (bootstrap discussion)

Next steps (owner: Asha):
- Convert this doc into a one-pager cheat sheet and a slide deck for the hands-on session by 2025-08-11.
- Create the minimal /examples repo and open PR against main.
- Run a dry-run with Solutions Eng (Marco) and record time-to-first-success metric.
